data.title: The tumor suppressor LKB1 kinase directly activates AMP-activated kinase and regulates apoptosis in response to energy stress
data.authors: Shaw RJ; Kosmatka M; Bardeesy N; Cantley LC et al.
data.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: LKB1-null MEFs; in vitro kinase assays
data.finding: The paper that identified LKB1 as the upstream kinase for AMPK: LKB1 directly phosphorylates AMPK-alpha on Thr172, and LKB1-null cells cannot activate AMPK under energy stress. This is the canonical source for the LKB1 -> AMPK step that gates the whole energy-sensing arm upstream of mTORC1.
data.abstract_excerpt: AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) is a highly conserved sensor of cellular energy status found in all eukaryotic cells. AMPK is activated by stimuli that increase the cellular AMP/ATP ratio. Essential to activation of AMPK is its phosphorylation at Thr-172 by an upstream kinase, AMPKK, whose identity in mammalian cells has remained elusive. Here we present biochemical and genetic evidence indicating that the LKB1 serine/threonine kinase, the gene inactivated in the Peutz-Jeghers familial cancer syndrome, is the dominant regulator of AMPK activation in several mammalian cell types.

extracted_findings.intervention: LKB1 loss (LKB1-null MEFs); in vitro phosphorylation of AMPK by LKB1
extracted_findings.species: Mouse embryonic fibroblasts; in vitro kinase assays
extracted_findings.effect: LKB1 directly phosphorylates and activates AMPK; without LKB1, AMPK is not activated by energy stress and cells are more prone to apoptosis
